# OSS 4008 — Project progress update

**November 9, 2026 \| Hospital Infrastructure in Canada**

My project aims to identify hospital infrastructure from overhead imagery and display the results on an interactive map of Canada. I've focused first on getting the mapping interface and the reference-data workflow working, so that I have a place to display and assess the model's results later.

## Completed so far

- Set up the Python Google Earth Engine environment in Google Colab and tested the initial imagery workflow.  
- Used Statistics Canada's Open Database of Healthcare Facilities (ODHF v2.0) as a national reference source. The notebook retrieved and filtered **678 hospital records** in its latest run.  
- Built a browser-based map with a Canadian city/town search, hospital markers, a study-radius setting and basic map navigation commands.  
- Explored candidate buildings around known hospital sites and prepared notebooks for annotation conversion and subsequent model training.  
- Organized the project into Colab notebooks, reusable Python app code, data references, future results and documentation.

## Current demonstration

Search for a city such as Kitchener or Ottawa and display the known hospital references within the chosen radius. The data points come from Statistics Canada, **not an AI model**. The app is running from Colab through a temporary Gradio link. The latest compact layout is prepared but still needs a final browser check.

![][image1]

## Next phase

My next priority is collecting licensed high-resolution overhead imagery and verifying labels for actual hospital buildings. I'll use the labelled images to train and test a detector, report measured performance and connect its predictions to a selected map area. The present study-area drawing tool isn't wired to inference yet.

## Issues to discuss

I need guidance on the shared frontend framework and whether Gradio is acceptable, the imagery sources and licences I can use, and the required annotation format. The course GitHub submission also needs to be kept current.

**Current status:** Working mapping/data-reference prototype; detector training and end-to-end imagery analysis are outstanding.
